data.name: Talora
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Talora means ‘dew from the earth,’ representing the refreshing and life-giving power of nature. In the Bible, this name is derived from the Talitha Cumi story where Jesus raises Jairus's daughter from the dead, symbolizing the power to bring new life and renewal.
data.numerology_meaning: A harmonious and loving nature, with a deep emotional sensitivity and understanding.

in_greek.name: Ταλωρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Η ονομασία Ταλωρα προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη θαυμαστής, η οποία αναφέρεται σε κάποιον που είναι θαυμάστης της χάριτος του Θεού. Η ονομασία αυτή είναι μια αναφορά στην ελαχιστοποίηση της δικής μας δόξας και την αναγνώριση της χάριτος που μας δίνεται από τον Θεό. Η Ταλωρα ήταν μια εκκλησιαστική ονομασία που χρησιμοποιούνταν κατά τη διάρκεια της πρώτης Χριστιανικής Εκκλησίας και αναφέρεται στην ιεραποστολή και την εξαγωγή της χάριτος του Θεού στον κόσμο.

in_latin.name: Talora
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Talora derivatur a vocabulo mirator, qui referatur ad aliquem qui est admirator gratiae Dei. Hoc nomen est referentia ad humilitatem nostram et recognitionem gratiae quae nobis dat Deus. Talora erat nomen ecclesiasticum quod in ecclesia prima Christiana usabatur et referabatur ad evangelizationem et distributionem gratiae Dei in mundum.

in_english.name: Talora
in_english.meaning: A person who marvels at God's grace
in_english.long_meaning: The name Talora originates from the Greek word 'thaumatistes', meaning 'one who marvels at God's grace'. This name is a reference to humbling oneself and recognizing the gift of grace given by God. In Christian tradition, the name Talora was used in the early church and refers to the evangelism and dissemination of God's grace to the world. It is a name that signifies a person who is in awe of God's mercy and is inspired to share it with others.

data.cultural_impact: The name Talora has potential ties to various Indo-European languages, but its meaning and origins are rooted in the Hebrew language. This connection to the ancient Hebrew language indicates a rich cultural background and history, common to many Christians.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Talora carries deep spiritual meaning, drawing inspiration from the Biblical story of Talitha Cumi. This story portrays the profound resurgence of life and the miraculous power of Jesus to give new life and healing to the dying. Therefore, the name Talora can be seen as a reminder of the renewing and revitalizing work of the Lord in our lives.

historical_references.reference: The name Talora is derived from the Latin name 'Talara', which means 'a place of rest'. It was used as a name for several Christian settlements throughout Europe during the Middle Ages. One such settlement was located in what is now modern-day Poland, and was established by German colonists in the late 13th century.

Another reference to the name Talora can be found in the works of English poet John Milton. In his epic poem 'Samson Agonistes', Milton mentions a character named Talora, who is described as a 'well-known virgin and prophetess' in the ancient city of Gaza. This reference dates back to the 17th century.
